segments.narration: A wave of beer killed eight people in London. Seventeenth of October, eighteen fourteen, in the St Giles rookery.
A seven-metre fermentation vat gave way. Its iron hoop had failed hours earlier and had been reported as nothing to worry about.
When it went, it took the other vats with it. More than half a million litres of porter hit the street at once.
St Giles was one of the poorest districts in the city, and families lived in basements. The beer poured straight down into them.
Eight people died, all women and children. The inquest called it an act of God, the brewery paid nothing, and it later got its excise duty refunded.
